items.title: iv. Surface tension and viscosity (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: iv. Surface tension and viscosity: a main subheading of 5.4.4 Influence of hydrogen bonding on the properties of water, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 103-103.

blocks.text: Pani ki surface tension aur viscosity bhi bohat zyada hain. Surface tension surface ke molecules par neeche ki taraf pull (khinchao) hai, jis se pani ka surface stretched (tana hua) rehta hai. Yeh pull andar ke molecules hydrogen bonds ke zariye lagate hain.

Viscosity liquid ka flow (behne) ke khilaf resistance (rukawat) hai. Pani ki viscosity bohat se liquids se zyada hai, jaise chhote hydrocarbons aur alcohols (maslan hexane aur ethanol). Wajah phir mazboot hydrogen bonds hain. Alcohols bhi hydrogen bond banate hain, magar pani se bohat kam aur kamzor; hydrocarbons hydrogen bond bana hi nahi sakte.

blocks.prompt: a) Kya CHF₃ hydrogen bond bana sakta hai? Kyun ya kyun nahi?
blocks.explanation: CHF₃ ke molecules aapas mein hydrogen bond nahi banate, kyunke us ka H carbon se jura hai, F, O ya N se nahi; is liye H par kaafi δ+ charge nahi aata. (Us ke F atoms kisi doosre molecule, jaise pani, ke H se bond le sakte hain.)

blocks.prompt: b) Ethanol ke do molecules ke darmiyan hydrogen bond dikhayein.
blocks.explanation: Ek ethanol molecule ka O−H wala H (δ+) doosre molecule ke O (δ−) ke lone pair ki taraf khinchta hai: CH₃CH₂−O−H ··· O(H)−CH₂CH₃. Dotted line hydrogen bond hai.

blocks.prompt: c) CH₃CH₂CH₃, CH₃CH₂OH aur CH₃CH₂Cl mein kaun si forces hain? Boiling point ka increasing order (barhti tarteeb) batayein.
blocks.explanation: Propane (CH₃CH₂CH₃): sirf London forces. Chloroethane (CH₃CH₂Cl): London + dipole-dipole forces. Ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH): London + dipole-dipole + hydrogen bonding. Order: CH₃CH₂CH₃ < CH₃CH₂Cl < CH₃CH₂OH.

blocks.prompt: d, e) Ethane (-89 ℃) aur methanol (65 ℃) ka farq 154 ℃ hai, magar butane (0 ℃) aur propanol (97 ℃) ka farq sirf 97 ℃. Molecule bara hone par farq kyun kam hota hai?
blocks.explanation: Dono pairs mein alcohol ka zyada boiling point us ke O−H group ke hydrogen bond se aata hai, jo har pair mein taqreeban utna hi hai. Lekin molecule bara hone se London forces barh jati hain aur total attraction ka bara hissa ban jati hain, is liye hydrogen bond ka extra asar muqable mein chhota reh jata hai aur farq ghat jata hai. (Kitab mein butane ka formula CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₄ chhapa hai; sahi CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ hai.)

blocks.prompt: f) Pure (khalis) acetic acid dimers ki shakal mein kyun hota hai magar aqueous solution (pani mein ghol) mein nahi?
blocks.explanation: Pure acetic acid mein do molecules apne COOH groups ke darmiyan do hydrogen bonds bana kar dimer (jora) ban jate hain. Pani mein acid ke O−H aur C=O groups aas paas ke bohat se pani ke molecules se hydrogen bonds bana lete hain, is liye dimer toot jate hain.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Quick Check 5.4 d) ii mein kitab butane ko “CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₄” likhti hai; aisa formula possible nahi (aakhri carbon ke paanch bond ho jate). Sahi CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ hai.

items: Barf: khali jagahon wala regular hydrogen-bonded network, 9% zyada volume, kam density, pani par tairti hai aur neeche ka pani bachati hai.
Pani ki specific heat capacity, heat of vaporization (41 kJ mol⁻¹), boiling point, surface tension aur viscosity sab zyada hain, wajah extensive hydrogen bonding.
